newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Rwandan genocide suspect arrested in Kenya.
newsitem.headline: Rwandan genocide suspect arrested in Kenya.

text.p: A former commander in Rwanda's ousted Hutu army has been arrested and transferred to the Rwanda genocide tribunal in northern Tanzania, the U.N. International Criminal Tribunal on Rwanda said on Wednesday.

In a statement, the tribunal said Samuel Manishimwe, a former commander in the town of Cyangugu during Rwanda's 1994 genocide, was arrested in the Kenyan coastal city of Mombasa on Tuesday and immediately transferred to the Tanzanian town of Arusha.
The statement said Manishimwe is suspected of committing genocide and crimes against humanity.
His arrest brings to 21 the number of people being held by the tribunal set by the United Nations Security Council to probe the 1994 slaughter of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus.
The tribunal will decide on Thursday whether to continue to detain six suspects earlier handed over by Kenya.
The six men would appear before its president, Judge Laity Kama of Senegal, in Arusha on Thursday for a decision on whether they should be released or their detention extended.
The tribunal said the six were among eight suspects arrested by Kenyan police in July and moved to the tribunal's headquarters in Arusha.

It said six of the eight were not indicted by the tribunal and were only suspected of having taken part in the 1994 genocide, sparked by the murder of Hutu military strongman Juvenal Habyarimana in April 1994.
The genocide was ended by Tutsi rebels who drove the Hutu army and militia into exile and took power in the tiny tea and coffee-growing nation.
The six were therefore only initially detained for 30 days.

The tribunal said the six included former prime minister Jean Kambanda, former newspaper editor Hassan Ngeze and Belgian Georges Ruggiu, a former journalist at Rwanda's Radio Television des Milles Collines and the only non-Rwandan held in Arusha.

The other three were Sylvain Nsabimana, a former government official in the southern Rwandan city of Butare, Gratien Kabiligi, a former colonel in the army's general staff, and Aloys Ntabakuze, former commander of a commando battalion.
Twenty-three suspects have been indicted and the tribunal held 20 in custody in Arusha up to Tuesday. Three trials are now in progress.
